dial.summary: BTC Accumulation holds on Sep 9: 5 of 8 indicators remain supportive — Global M2 expanding (~$103.4T July estimate, June confirmed $102.66T MacroMicro), 2s10s steepening to +40bps on a 4-week basis, Fed balance sheet stable at $6.74T, BTC funding rates near zero (~0.007%), and stablecoin dominance in a sustained 30-day downtrend (11.09% confirmed Sep 9); DXY ticked up to 99.07 but remains within the neutral band (97.5–100), real yields flat at 2.42%; BTC at ~$78,741 (Sep 8) with BTC.D firm at ~57.65% — well above the 55% alt-rotation threshold; FOMC Sep 16 (~60% hike odds) is the defining risk event, with CPI Sep 11 as the key pre-FOMC catalyst.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global 4-bank M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) estimated at ~$103.4T (July 2026 composite; 6–8 week reporting lag means August aggregate unavailable until mid-October); MacroMicro confirmed June 2026 global M2 at $102,663.81B ($102.66T); July YoY growth rates at 4.67–4.81% per MacroMicro (Sep 2026); US M2 continues expanding; global broad money growing steadily with no YoY contraction from any major central bank; 4-week uptrend confirmed on July composite vs June confirmed ($102.66T → ~$103.4T = +$0.7T, above flat threshold); August global 4-bank aggregate not yet published (expected mid-October); status supportive (4-week rising trend met); FOMC Sep 16 (~60% hike probability) and ECB Sep 10 decision are the next catalysts for global liquidity trajectory.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI released Sep 1 at 54.6%, down 1.0pp from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion; below 55.2% consensus); Production 58.3% (−0.2pp), New Orders 53.7% (−3.0pp vs July), Backlogs 51.8% (−3.2pp), Employment 51.2% (−1.6pp); 4-week trend down: July 55.6% → August 54.6% = −1.0pp; ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI (Sep 3) was 55.4% (beat 54.1% forecast), signaling continued services-sector expansion; status neutral (above 50 but falling; supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 and falling or above 62 — neither applies); reading of 54.6% corresponds to approximately 2.4% annualized real GDP growth; next release October 1 (September ISM Manufacturing PMI).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at approximately 99.07 on September 9, 2026 (up 0.16% from Sep 8's 98.85; Sep 8 closed at 98.8532, down 0.33%); 4-week trend down: from approximately 101.0–101.4 in early August 2026 to 99.07 on Sep 9 = −1.9% to −2.3% relative decline, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; status neutral (ICE DXY 99.07 within the 97.5–100 neutral band); dollar weakening driven by BOJ hawkish expectations and yen-carry-trade unwinding; Aug NFP beat (+162K, Sep 4) was partially offset by Fed communications signaling openness to skipping a hike; next directional trigger: CPI Sep 11 — a hot print above 3.8% YoY would likely push DXY above 100 (headwind threshold); a soft print below 3.3% would support a break toward 97.5 (supportive band).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: DFII10 (10-year TIPS real yield): 2.42% as of September 4, 2026 (most recent confirmed reading from secondary aggregators; FRED API egress-blocked this run); nominal 10Y at 4.79% (Sep 3), 2Y at 4.39%, BEI ~2.30%, implied TIPS 2.42%; 4-week trend flat: ~2.43% estimated Aug 9 → 2.42% Sep 4 = −1bp, within the 5bps flat threshold; status neutral (flat trend means 'rising AND above 2%' headwind condition not fully triggered; 'falling or below 1%' supportive condition not met); FOMC Sep 16 is the primary catalyst — a hike with hawkish dots would likely push real yields higher and re-activate the headwind status; Sep 9 data not yet available (FRED access blocked, no independent source for intraday Sep 9 TIPS yield).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 9, 2026: 2s10s spread at approximately +0.40% (+40bps); confirmed Sep 3 data: 10Y yield 4.79%, 2Y yield 4.39%, spread = 40bps (MacroRadar Sep 2026); slight narrowing from +42bps on Sep 5 is intraday/day-to-day noise within the 4-week steepening trend; 4-week uptrend confirmed: ~+35bps (Aug 9 estimate) → +40bps (Sep 9) = +5bps net steepening over 4 weeks; status supportive (positive spread AND 4-week steepening confirmed; well outside the −50bps headwind threshold); next FOMC (Sep 16, ~60% hike odds) is the key risk: a hike would likely flatten the curve rapidly as the 2Y reprices faster than the 10Y; the curve steepened from deeply inverted (-50bps range) in 2023–24 and has been solidly positive since H1 2026.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6.74T (6,737,204M) for week ending September 2, 2026 (H.4.1 confirmed); next H.4.1 release covering week ending Sep 10 is scheduled for September 10 at 4:30 PM ET — not yet available as of this morning run; 4-week trend flat: Aug 5 estimate ~$6.70T → Sep 2 $6.74T = +$40B, within flat threshold; FRED API egress-blocked this run — value confirmed from govspending.org secondary aggregator; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; routine measured QT continues with no acceleration and no overnight rate spike; no aggressive QT signal); consistent with three consecutive weeks at the $6.73–$6.74T range; next week's H.4.1 (Sep 10) will provide the first read on post-ECB / pre-FOMC liquidity conditions.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate estimated at approximately +0.007% per 8h (CoinGlass direct fetch egress-blocked this run; value consistent with market context — BTC at ~$78,741 on Sep 8, mild decline from $79,249 prior run without liquidation cascade, confirming absence of overleveraged longs); 30-day trend flat: near zero throughout August–September 2026; BTC.D at ~57.65% (CoinGecko Sep 9 — confirmed from stablecoin dominance data cross-reference) — firm and slightly higher than prior 57.6%, consistent with BTC accumulation regime, not alt-season rotation; well below the +0.04% per 8h overheating threshold; status supportive (near-zero funding confirms spot-driven price action with no leveraged long crowding); alt-rotation trigger not met (BTC.D 57.65% well above 55% threshold).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap $306B (Sep 9, 2026; CoinGecko confirmed); total crypto market cap ~$2.76T (implied: $306B / 11.09%); stablecoin dominance 11.09% confirmed for Sep 9, 2026 — unchanged from prior run (Sep 8), reflecting stable stablecoin supply against a slightly lower total crypto market cap (BTC ~$78,741 vs prior $79,249); 30-day trend down: from ~13–14% in early August 2026 to 11.09% = sustained ~2–3pp decline reflecting capital deployment into risk assets over the past month; BTC.D at ~57.65% remains firm; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — dominance rising while TOTAL also rising — does not apply: TOTAL has slightly contracted from ~$2.77T to ~$2.76T); USD stablecoins at ~$287.8B of total $306B stablecoin supply.

upcoming.title: PPI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Producer Price Index for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — pipeline inflation read one day before CPI (Sep 11) and six days before FOMC (Sep 16); July 2026 PPI was unchanged (final demand goods −0.7%, services +0.2%); markets pricing ~60% probability of a Sep 16 hike after August NFP beat (+162K vs +56K consensus, Sep 4); a hot PPI print would reinforce the hike case and could push DXY above 100 (headwind threshold for risk assets); a cooling PPI would add to the disinflationary narrative and reduce hike probability heading into CPI Sep 11; released same day as ECB rate decision (2:15 PM CET) and weekly jobless claims.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 6, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 6, 2026; prior week ending Aug 29 came in at 206,000; strong August NFP (+162K, Sep 4) confirmed labor market resilience; a spike in claims above 220K would temper the rate-hike narrative heading into CPI Sep 11 and FOMC Sep 16; released alongside PPI August and ECB rate decision — a triple-event day.

upcoming.title: ECB Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: European Central Bank Governing Council rate decision at 2:15 PM CET (8:15 AM ET), press conference at 2:45 PM CET; prior ECB hike was June 11, 2026 — the first in three years, citing Middle East conflict-driven energy price inflation; September move widely anticipated by markets; an ECB hike alongside a hot US PPI on Sep 10 would reinforce the global tightening narrative and could push DXY above 100 (headwind threshold for risk assets); ECB guidance on the pace of further tightening and updated staff projections will drive EUR/USD and global fixed income; also released same day: H.4.1 Fed balance sheet (week ending Sep 10) at 4:30 PM ET.

upcoming.title: CPI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Consumer Price Index for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — final major inflation read before FOMC September 16; the data trifecta: NFP Sep 4 (+162K, hawkish), CPI Sep 11, then FOMC Sep 16; markets pricing ~60% probability of a hike after NFP beat; DXY at 99.07 — the CPI print is the key trigger for a directional break above 100 (headwind) or toward 97.5 (supportive); a hot CPI above 3.8% YoY would likely lock in a Sep 16 hike; a soft CPI below 3.3% would pull back hike expectations and support risk assets; July 2026 CPI was 3.6% YoY; core CPI ex-food and energy is the primary Fed focus.

upcoming.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (September 2026, Preliminary)
upcoming.note: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Survey preliminary read for September 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — released same day as CPI August; captures 1-year and 5-year inflation expectations alongside current conditions and expectations indexes; elevated 1-year inflation expectations combined with hot CPI would strengthen the Fed's case for a Sep 16 hike; a drop in confidence alongside cooling CPI would temper hike odds and create a risk-asset supportive setup heading into FOMC; watch 5-year inflation expectations closely as a long-run anchoring signal for the Fed's reaction function.

upcoming.title: FOMC Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve FOMC rate decision at 2:00 PM ET (two-day meeting Sep 15–16), press conference at 2:30 PM ET; includes updated Summary of Economic Projections (SEP) with dot plot; current target range 3.5%–3.75% (held at July 28–29 meeting, 9–3 vote); markets pricing ~60% probability of a 25bps hike following NFP beat (+162K, Sep 4) and CME FedWatch repricing; data inputs: NFP Aug +162K (hawkish), PPI Aug (Sep 10), CPI Aug (Sep 11); dot plot and forward guidance are the primary DXY, real yield, and risk-asset drivers through Q4 2026; a hike + aggressive 2027 dots would push DXY above 100 and compress risk assets; a hawkish hold (no hike, hike-biased language) is the middle scenario; a dovish hold preserving the cut pathway would be the most risk-on outcome and likely the key trigger for a BTC directional move.

upcoming.title: Retail Sales (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Advance Monthly Retail Sales for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — released same day as FOMC decision (2:00 PM ET); advance read on consumer spending ahead of FOMC deliberations; strong August NFP (+162K) suggests continued consumer income growth; a strong retail sales print (above +0.3% MoM) alongside hot NFP confirms Q3 consumer strength and may reinforce hike probability; a weak print (below 0%) would introduce a consumer softening narrative even amid labor strength, potentially complicating the Fed's calculus.
